prose: A New York Times analysis argues that Nvidia's leadership crisis could matter beyond one company because its chips, financing relationships and customers sit near the center of the AI investment boom. It links uncertainty over management to existing doubts about the returns on data-center spending. This is a macroeconomic risk argument, not a demonstration that a leadership change will necessarily interrupt growth.
highlights: Nvidia connects chip supply and infrastructure financing
Article examines dependence on one executive
Leadership uncertainty meets existing return concerns
Macroeconomic effects are a possibility, not certainty
Analysis should be distinguished from confirmed outcomes
